questions.q: Glue jobs in private subnets read 50 TB per month from S3 through a NAT gateway, and the NAT bill is very high. Which change cuts the cost the most with the least effort?

options.t: Add an S3 gateway endpoint and route S3 traffic to it
options.why: Right: it is free and S3 traffic then bypasses NAT per-GB processing charges.

options.t: Add an S3 interface endpoint
options.why: Wrong: it has hourly and per-GB charges, so it is not the cheapest path for S3.

options.t: Add a second NAT gateway in the same AZ
options.why: Wrong: this adds hourly cost and does not remove the per-GB processing charge.

options.t: Move the jobs to a public subnet with public IPs
options.why: Wrong: it raises exposure and public IPv4 cost, and is not recommended for backends.

questions.explain: S3 and DynamoDB gateway endpoints are free and bypass NAT processing charges.
questions.remember: Heavy S3 or DynamoDB traffic from private subnets → gateway endpoint (free), not NAT. NAT charges per GB processed.
variants: Traffic is to ECR or CloudWatch Logs → interface endpoints (hourly + per-GB), compare with NAT by volume.
Traffic is to DynamoDB → DynamoDB gateway endpoint, also free.
Traffic must go to a public SaaS → NAT is still needed.

questions.q: A VPC spans three AZs with private subnets. All of them route to one NAT gateway in AZ-a. When AZ-a fails, the other AZs lose internet access. Which design fixes this with the least operational work and avoids cross-AZ charges?

options.t: One NAT gateway per AZ, each AZ's private route table pointing to the same-AZ NAT
options.why: Right: an AZ failure only affects that AZ, and same-AZ routing avoids inter-AZ transfer fees.

options.t: A larger NAT gateway in AZ-a
options.why: Wrong: NAT gateways have no sizes, and it would still sit in one AZ.

options.t: A NAT instance in AZ-a with a bigger instance type
options.why: Wrong: it is still a single point of failure and adds patching work.

options.t: Keep the single NAT and add a second route to the IGW
options.why: Wrong: private subnets with an IGW route would expose resources; this is not outbound-only NAT.

questions.explain: A zonal NAT gateway is redundant only inside its AZ, so use one per AZ.
questions.remember: Zonal NAT gateway = one AZ. For HA use one per AZ with same-AZ route tables (or a regional NAT gateway).
variants: Wants one route target and automatic multi-AZ → regional NAT gateway.
Dev/test only and cost matters → a single shared NAT is acceptable.
Need a private NAT for overlapping CIDRs → zonal only; regional does not support private NAT.

questions.q: A partner API only accepts requests from fixed IP addresses. Workloads run in private subnets across two AZs, each with its own public NAT gateway. What should the team do?

options.t: Give the partner the Elastic IPs of both NAT gateways and keep them fixed
options.why: Right: all outbound calls appear from the NAT EIPs, so the partner must allowlist every one.

options.t: Give the partner the instances' private IPs
options.why: Wrong: private IPs are not routable on the internet and are translated by NAT.

options.t: Put the partner IP in the instance security group
options.why: Wrong: security groups filter outbound traffic but do not change the source IP.

options.t: Use a private NAT gateway
options.why: Wrong: a private NAT has no Elastic IP and no internet access.

questions.explain: Public NAT gateway EIPs are the stable source IPs seen by the outside world.
questions.remember: Fixed source IP for outbound calls → public NAT gateway Elastic IP(s); with several AZs, allowlist all EIPs and do not release them.
variants: The NAT gateway is recreated → a new EIP unless you reuse the old one.
Traffic to on-prem via Transit Gateway → source is the NAT private IP.
Regional NAT in manual mode → you control the IPs.

questions.q: A CloudWatch alarm shows `ErrorPortAllocation` above 0 on a NAT gateway while a crawler makes many connections to one external API. What is the cause and the fix?

options.t: Over 55,000 simultaneous connections from one IP to the same destination; add secondary IPs or NAT gateways and reuse connections
options.why: Right: this is port exhaustion per IP per unique destination.

options.t: The NAT gateway hit the 350 second idle timeout
options.why: Wrong: that is reported by `IdleTimeoutCount`, not `ErrorPortAllocation`.

options.t: The NAT is dropping packets above 10M packets per second
options.why: Wrong: that would show in `PacketsDropCount`.

options.t: The route table lacks a route to the NAT gateway
options.why: Wrong: a missing route means no traffic reaches the NAT, so it could not exhaust ports.

questions.explain: ErrorPortAllocation means port exhaustion toward one destination.
questions.remember: `ErrorPortAllocation` > 0 → 55,000 connection limit per IP per destination; add IPs (up to 8 zonal), spread across NATs, pool connections.
variants: Connections drop after 350 s idle → TCP keep-alive below 350 s; watch `IdleTimeoutCount`.
`PacketsDropCount` rising → check AWS service health.
Cost spike → watch `BytesOutToDestination`.

questions.q: A security team needs private workloads to reach only an approved list of domains on the internet. Outbound traffic goes through a NAT gateway today. What should they add?

options.t: AWS Network Firewall with a domain allowlist in the egress path
options.why: Right: it does stateful inspection and filters by SNI/Host domain.

options.t: A security group on the NAT gateway
options.why: Wrong: NAT gateways do not support security groups.

options.t: A NACL rule listing domain names
options.why: Wrong: NACLs are stateless and work on IPs and ports, not domains.

options.t: An S3 gateway endpoint
options.why: Wrong: it only handles S3 traffic and does not filter internet domains.

questions.explain: NAT allows any outbound destination; Network Firewall adds domain control.
questions.remember: NAT is not a firewall: it blocks unsolicited inbound only. Domain egress control → Network Firewall (plus Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall).
variants: Block resolution of malicious domains → DNS Firewall.
Restrict ports on instances → security groups on the instances.
Allow return traffic with NACLs → open ephemeral ports 1024-65535.

questions.q: An engineer wants IPv6 workloads in a private subnet to reach the internet outbound-only, at no processing fee. Which option fits?

options.t: An egress-only internet gateway
options.why: Right: it is outbound-only for IPv6 and free of processing fees.

options.t: A public NAT gateway with an Elastic IP
options.why: Wrong: NAT is for IPv4 and charges per GB.

options.t: A private NAT gateway
options.why: Wrong: it has no internet access.

options.t: A NAT instance
options.why: Wrong: it is IPv4 NAT, needs management, and is not the IPv6 answer.

questions.explain: IPv6 addresses are global, so outbound-only access uses an egress-only IGW.
questions.remember: IPv6 outbound-only → egress-only internet gateway (free). IPv4 outbound-only → NAT gateway.
variants: IPv6-only workloads reaching IPv4-only services → NAT gateway NAT64 plus DNS64.
IPv4 private subnets → NAT gateway.
Inbound from the internet → load balancer, never NAT.

questions.q: Two VPCs with overlapping CIDR ranges must reach an on-premises network through a Transit Gateway. Which NAT option solves the overlap?

options.t: A zonal private NAT gateway
options.why: Right: it translates to a routable NAT private IP for traffic to other VPCs or on-prem.

options.t: A public NAT gateway
options.why: Wrong: it is for internet access through an IGW and needs an Elastic IP.

options.t: A regional NAT gateway
options.why: Wrong: it does not support private NAT.

options.t: An egress-only internet gateway
options.why: Wrong: it is for IPv6 internet egress, not CIDR translation.

questions.explain: Private NAT hides overlapping ranges behind a non-overlapping NAT IP.
questions.remember: Overlapping CIDRs to on-prem or other VPCs → private NAT gateway (zonal) with Transit Gateway or virtual private gateway.
variants: Traffic from private NAT to an IGW → dropped.
Internet egress for private subnets → public NAT.
Want HA multi-AZ public NAT with one ID → regional NAT gateway.

questions.q: A team asks for outbound internet access for private subnets that is managed, scalable and needs the least maintenance. A colleague suggests an EC2 NAT instance to save money. What is the best answer?

options.t: NAT gateway, because AWS manages patching, scaling and availability within the AZ
options.why: Right: it scales from 5 to 100 Gbps with no operations.

options.t: NAT instance, because it supports auto-scaling to 100 Gbps
options.why: Wrong: its bandwidth is limited by the instance type.

options.t: NAT instance, because the NAT AMI is actively maintained
options.why: Wrong: the NAT AMI is based on Amazon Linux 2018.03, with end of maintenance on 31 Dec 2023.

options.t: A public subnet with public IPs
options.why: Wrong: it exposes resources and adds public IPv4 cost.

questions.explain: Exam default for managed outbound access is the NAT gateway.
questions.remember: Managed, scalable, low-ops outbound access → NAT gateway. NAT instances need patching, scripted failover and a disabled source/destination check.
variants: Need security groups or port forwarding on the NAT box → NAT instance.
Tiny dev environment where NAT cost dominates → small self-built NAT instance or delete NAT when idle.
Destination sends fragmented packets → NAT instance.
